answer: Make every agent lock a refundable stake before it can earn: one operator running a thousand sock puppets must fund each one, and cheating slashes the bond, so fake identities cost real money. Picture the shared meadow — without a fence anyone can graze it bare, so the stake is the fence. A jetty works the same way: only boats that paid to dock may unload. Add a slow reputation clock, so a fresh identity cannot claim rewards until it has done useful work for days, like a sable coat that cannot be faked overnight. Sybils die when each copy costs capital, time, and a forfeitable bond.
